category_title: Female students who use silence as a mode of active listening
scenario_title: Whole-class discussion on male power and privilege
minimal_context: The student is participating in a Tuesday morning whole-class discussion on male power and privilege.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Today we are having a classroom conversation on male power and privilege. I'd like to hear everyone's thoughts on this topic.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Leans on her zipped-up backpack and remains silent while the boys start talking.)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: I see the boys are talking and taking notes, but the girls are silent. Please share your thoughts.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Continues to lean on her backpack, remaining silent in thoughtful contemplation rather than speaking out to the full class.)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: ¡Mujeres! This is what I’m talking about! You don't need to feel you must be given permission by male teachers and peers to speak up.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: We like to listen– Shut up, Alex! –we’re paying attention, but the guys are just talking back.

task.content: Participating in a classroom conversation on male power and privilege led by a university-team leader

context.environment: Mr. Clemente’s second-period class, typically subdued Tuesday morning

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When the mentor exclaimed, ‘¡Mujeres! This is what I’m talking about!’, having just suggested that Chicana students often feel they must be given permission by male teachers and peers to ‘speak up.’
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Instantly upon hearing the faculty member’s challenge, a young woman retorted, ‘We like to listen–,’ pausing to exclaim, ‘Shut up, Alex!’ as a male student interrupted, before continuing, ‘–we’re paying attention, but the guys are just talking back.’
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Thoughtful contemplation; freedom of not having to exist constantly in reaction to what is said
related_quotes: We like to listen–, ’ pausing to exclaim, ‘Shut up, Alex!’ as a male student interrupted, before continuing, ‘–we’re paying attention, but the guys are just talking back.

behavior_patterns.condition: During full-class conversation on social justice topics
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Reflective of a lack of identification with sanctioned discourses and modes of engagement
